A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TetraSDF, despite the revised subtitle and formatting. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, self-consistency, preconditioning and runtime experiments on Stanford, ABC and Thingi10K, with additional qualitative results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original field-accuracy, baseline-capacity, adaptive-extraction and triangle-quality results.

M1.justification: The tetrahedral encoder, input preconditioner, skeleton construction, region tracking, edge subdivision and face extraction remain unchanged. The new grid-design discussion and Algorithm 1 explain existing choices rather than introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SDF learning and isosurface extraction on the same Stanford shapes, 100 ABC meshes and 500 closed Thingi10K meshes. The added metrics, model configurations and extraction algorithms do not introduce new data domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix A.5.3/Table A4 adds evaluated comparisons against octree Marching Cubes, octree Dual Contouring and McGrids. Original comparators remain. The MC256-to-MT256 correction in v1 Table 6/v2 Table 5 fixes a mislabeled existing row rather than adding a comparator.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include SDF MAE at one million ground-truth surface samples, AM configurations with 15/150 and 20/200 hidden-layer/width settings, adaptive extraction from the same Large network, and the fraction of faces with minimum angle below 5 degrees. Existing training settings and original evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds analysis separating field fitting from extraction error, AM capacity/runtime sensitivity, a depth-12 octree failure case, and triangle-regularity assessment. Existing preconditioner ablations and resolution studies remain; the original runtime breakdown and Dragon comparison are relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors or significance tests. The added averages across shapes do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are retained, but substantial new results appear in Table 3 and Tables A3–A5. For example, Large/Stanford SDF MAE is 0.62 for TetraSDF versus 0.53 for HashGrid, in units of 10^-3. Newly reported skinny-face fractions are 11.83% for TetraSDF, 10.05% for AM and 10.94% for TropicalNeRF.

T1.justification: Appendix A.6.2 adds a mathematical argument that HashGrid's cube-average interpolation metric is proportional to the identity, so volume-preserving isotropization admits the identity preconditioner. Existing affine-interpolation and convexity proofs, and the tetrahedral preconditioner derivation, are retained.

C1.justification: Exact extraction, expressive SDF learning and encoder-specific preconditioning remain the central claims. v2 explicitly elevates tensorized GPU construction to a contribution and qualifies the conclusion from surpassing grid-based encoders to matching or surpassing them, consistent with the existing abstract.

C2.justification: New discussions explain the six-tetrahedron design relative to five- and twelve-tetrahedron alternatives, why the preconditioner does not benefit HashGrid, and the tradeoff between exact field agreement and triangle regularity. v2 also interprets capacity and adaptive-extraction results and identifies downstream editing limitations absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and identifies publicly released baseline implementations, CGAL implementations for sampling-based extractors, and McGrids' official defaults. These are additional access and implementation disclosures; the existing training and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to CGAL, power-diagram isosurfacing, McGrids, Reach for the Spheres, Flexible Isosurface Extraction and Marching Neurons. Related work expands its discussion of finite-sample and adaptive extraction while retaining the original positioning around exact CPWA extraction.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introductory motivation and conclusion receive targeted revisions; related-work subsections and experimental material are reordered. Appendix A.7 adds explanatory notation and pseudocode. Most method and proof exposition remains intact, so the language changes are limited rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column formatting, with extensive rearrangement of tables and figures. v2 adds a conceptual extraction schematic, four result tables and an algorithm display, revises overview annotations, and relocates the runtime table. Existing qualitative image content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps: Table 3 separates field accuracy from extraction error, while Tables A3–A4 test larger AM networks and adaptive extractors missing from v1. The quantified triangle-regularity limitation makes applicability clearer without representing a deterioration of the method. Together these additions substantially strengthen evidence and transparency, although adaptive-extractor settings remain sparsely documented.
